accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: accused from the rival group in the same village; dispute over the marriage settlement of the victim's granddaughter
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.149 (trial); IPC ss.147, 148 r/w s.149; IPC ss.337, 504 r/w s.149 (acquitted at trial); on appeal, IPC s.302 r/w s.34
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (three witnesses); medical evidence (post-mortem and injury examination by doctors); police complaint/FIR
aggravating_circumstances: Group assault by several accused, with axe and sticks; fatal head injury attributed to the accused armed with an axe
trial_court_outcome: Convicted six of eleven accused under s.302 r/w s.149 IPC; life imprisonment and fine of Rs. 500 each; no separate sentence for ss.147/148 r/w s.149
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction of A-1, A-2 and A-7 under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC and life sentence confirmed; A-3, A-4 and A-10 acquitted by benefit of doubt
offence_finally_established: Murder: IPC s.302 read with s.34
neutral_facts: On a morning at about 7 a.m., the victim went to a nearby house to discuss the proposed marriage of his granddaughter to a son of the woman of that house. After the discussion, as the victim came out, a group of persons who had been sitting in another nearby house came out, approached him, scolded him about the marriage arrangement, and assaulted him with an axe, stones and sticks. Several relatives and villagers who came to rescue the victim were also assaulted and sustained injuries. The attack ended after police intervention. The victim was taken by bullock cart to a hospital and then referred to a civil hospital, where he died the same evening, about twelve hours after the assault. He remained unconscious throughout that time and no dying declaration was recorded. A complaint was lodged with the police later that night. The doctor who conducted the post-mortem stated that the probable cause of death was primarily head injury associated with other multiple injuries, and that some stick injuries and an axe injury were identified. Doctors examined the injuries of some accused and found them minor. Eyewitness testimony came from the victim's brother, who was also injured, the victim's son, who witnessed the occurrence, and the mother-in-law of the granddaughter's fiancé, each describing the overt acts of particular accused.
physical_harm: Death of the victim (head injury with multiple injuries); injuries to two eyewitnesses who tried to rescue him; minor injuries to some accused
number_of_offences: 5 charged (ss.302, 147, 148, 337, 504 IPC); 1 finally upheld (s.302 r/w s.34 IPC)
motive: alleged: dispute over the marriage settlement of the victim's granddaughter, with the accused objecting that the match was made to gain support
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PWs 3, 4 and 5; post-mortem evidence of PW-1 attributing head injury to A-7 (axe) and other injuries to A-1 and A-2 (sticks/axe); PW-2's evidence that the accused's injuries were minor
witness_credibility: Related witnesses (brother, son, mother-in-law) found credible; relationship alone not a ground to reject, testimony scrutinised and found free of infirmity; injured witnesses' presence not doubted
trial_duration: offence: 19.01.1992; trial judgment: 19.07.2003; High Court: 11.04.2005; Supreme Court: 27.09.2012
legal_representation: Accused: Vikas Upadhyay (Crl. A. 246/2008) and Brij Bhusan (Crl. A. 247/2008). State: Sushil Karanjakar
investigation_status: FIR/complaints registered (Crime Nos. 6/92 and 7/92); cases committed to Sessions Court; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Delay in lodging the complaint, no dying declaration recorded, and no explanation for injuries to some accused were raised; the court held none of these affected the prosecution case
appeal_history: Trial court: six convicted under s.302 r/w s.149, life imprisonment. High Court: appeal dismissed as to A-1, A-2 and A-7 (s.302 r/w s.34), A-3, A-4 and A-10 acquitted. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: Evidence properly appreciated; eyewitnesses were injured; conviction under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC should not be disturbed
defence_argument: Witnesses are relatives of the deceased; FIR delay unexplained; no dying declaration; injuries to accused unexplained, suggesting a free fight, so the prosecution story should be disbelieved
legal_principle_applied: Relatives' testimony is not to be discarded merely for relationship but must be carefully scrutinised; delay, missing dying declaration and minor unexplained injuries do not defeat the prosecution where explained by circumstances; common intention under s.34
precedent_relied_upon: Abdul Rashid Abdul Rahiman Patel and Ors. v. State of Maharashtra (2007) 9 SCC 1
